parts.name: Google Pixel 10 Pro / Pro XL, 16GB
parts.software_stack: Android; on-device NN APIs; Vulkan; app-local runtimes such as llama.cpp-compatible ports where supported
parts.plain_language: Pixel 10 Pro provides 16GB RAM in a phone-sized power envelope. Android is more flexible than iOS for experimentation but thermal throttling and mobile process limits still make it an endpoint rather than a normal server node.
parts.source_notes: Google's current technical specifications list Tensor G5 and 16GB RAM. No tokens/sec or wall-power claim is inferred from the SoC specification.

parts.name: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, up to 16GB
parts.software_stack: Android; Vulkan; vendor/mobile NN APIs; app/local CLI runtimes where supported
parts.plain_language: Galaxy S26 Ultra has 12GB on common storage tiers and a 16GB 1TB configuration, making it a useful Android local-inference reference. It remains thermally and OS constrained compared with a desktop node.
parts.source_notes: Samsung documents 12GB RAM on 256/512GB models and 16GB on the 1TB model, with Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy. Charging wattage is not treated as inference power.
